official_outline_path: Disorders of puberty and sexual development
blueprint.primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts

item.vignette: A 16-year-old boy is evaluated because he has not entered puberty. He has minimal facial and axillary hair, small testes, and a high-pitched voice. He says that he has never been able to smell food or perfume. Serum testosterone is low, and luteinizing hormone and follicle-stimulating hormone are also low. Prolactin is normal. His maternal uncle had similar findings.
item.lead_in: Which of the following developmental abnormalities most directly explains this patient's findings?

options.A: Failure of anti-Müllerian hormone signaling in the fetal Müllerian ducts
options.B: Failure of gonadotropin-releasing hormone neurons to migrate from the developing nasal region to the forebrain
options.C: Failure of androgen-receptor complexes to regulate target-gene transcription
options.D: Failure to convert testosterone to dihydrotestosterone in reproductive tissues
options.E: Failure of 17-alpha-hydroxylase and 17,20-lyase activity in steroidogenic tissues

explanation.key_explanation: Kallmann syndrome combines hypogonadotropic hypogonadism with anosmia because developmentally linked olfactory neurons and GnRH-producing neurons fail to migrate normally from the developing nasal region toward the forebrain. Low GnRH produces low LH/FSH and low testosterone.

distractor_explanations.A: Defective AMH/AMHR2 signaling causes persistence of Müllerian structures in a 46,XY individual; it does not cause anosmia with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.
distractor_explanations.B: Correct. Disrupted migration of olfactory and GnRH-producing neurons explains both anosmia and low gonadotropins.
distractor_explanations.C: Androgen-receptor dysfunction causes androgen insensitivity despite androgen production and does not explain anosmia with low LH/FSH.
distractor_explanations.D: SRD5A2 deficiency impairs conversion of testosterone to DHT and primarily alters androgen-dependent external genital development; it does not cause anosmia or central hypogonadism.
distractor_explanations.E: CYP17A1 deficiency impairs steroid synthesis and is associated with hypertension/hypokalemia and deficient sex steroids, not the anosmia-central hypogonadism pattern.

explanation.educational_objective: Associate Kallmann syndrome with failed embryonic migration of olfactory and GnRH-producing neurons, causing anosmia and hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.

evidence_map.claim: Kallmann syndrome reflects disrupted migration of olfactory and GnRH-producing neurons.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Explains anosmia plus low LH/FSH/testosterone.

evidence_map.claim: Failure of AMH signaling causes persistence of Müllerian structures rather than Kallmann syndrome.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Does not fit the anosmia-hypogonadotropic phenotype.

evidence_map.claim: AR variants impair tissue response to androgens.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Does not explain low gonadotropins with anosmia.

evidence_map.claim: SRD5A2 converts testosterone to DHT and its deficiency alters male external genital development.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Mechanistically distinct from failed GnRH-neuron migration.

evidence_map.claim: CYP17A1 deficiency causes impaired glucocorticoid/sex-steroid synthesis with mineralocorticoid excess.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Expected phenotype differs from anosmic central hypogonadism.

item.vignette: A 17-year-old girl is evaluated for primary amenorrhea. She has normal breast development, sparse pubic and axillary hair, and a short blind-ending vagina. Pelvic ultrasonography shows no uterus; gonadal tissue is present in the inguinal canals. Karyotype is 46,XY, and serum testosterone is within the typical adult male range.
item.lead_in: Which of the following molecular abnormalities most directly explains this patient's phenotype?

options.A: Loss of steroid 5-alpha-reductase 2 activity with impaired conversion of testosterone to dihydrotestosterone
options.B: Loss of anti-Müllerian hormone receptor signaling in Müllerian duct cells
options.C: Failure of gonadotropin-releasing hormone neurons to migrate to the hypothalamus
options.D: Loss of androgen-receptor function with impaired androgen-dependent gene transcription
options.E: Loss of 17-alpha-hydroxylase and 17,20-lyase activity with reduced sex-steroid synthesis

item.tested_construct: Molecular mechanism of complete androgen insensitivity syndrome

explanation.key_explanation: Complete androgen insensitivity syndrome is caused by loss-of-function variants in the X-linked AR gene. A 46,XY individual forms testes and AMH, so Müllerian structures regress, but target tissues cannot respond to testosterone/DHT, producing female-typical external anatomy and sparse androgen-dependent hair.

distractor_explanations.A: 5-alpha-reductase deficiency lowers DHT but preserves testosterone action; virilization commonly increases at puberty and the mechanism is enzymatic rather than receptor resistance.
distractor_explanations.B: Loss of AMH signaling would cause persistence of a uterus and fallopian tubes, opposite the absent uterus here.
distractor_explanations.C: Kallmann syndrome causes low GnRH/LH/FSH and low gonadal sex steroids, not male-range testosterone in a 46,XY person.
distractor_explanations.D: Correct. Nonfunctional androgen receptors prevent androgen-response gene transcription despite adequate testosterone.
distractor_explanations.E: CYP17A1 deficiency lowers sex-steroid production and commonly produces mineralocorticoid excess with hypertension/hypokalemia; testosterone would not be in the adult male range.

explanation.educational_objective: Recognize complete androgen insensitivity as androgen-receptor loss of function in a 46,XY individual with testes, absent Müllerian structures, female-typical external anatomy, normal breasts, and sparse pubic hair.

evidence_map.claim: AR variants cause androgen insensitivity by impairing receptor binding/function and androgen-regulated gene activity.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Fits 46,XY, male-range testosterone, absent uterus, female external phenotype, sparse hair.

evidence_map.claim: SRD5A2 deficiency specifically impairs testosterone-to-DHT conversion.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Different molecular lesion from global androgen-receptor resistance.

evidence_map.claim: AMH/AMHR2 loss causes persistent Müllerian structures.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Contradicted by absent uterus.

evidence_map.claim: Kallmann syndrome is a GnRH-neuron migration disorder causing hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Contradicted by male-range testosterone.

evidence_map.claim: CYP17A1 deficiency reduces sex-steroid synthesis and produces mineralocorticoid excess.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Does not fit preserved male-range testosterone.

item.vignette: A 14-year-old child with a 46,XY karyotype was raised as a girl after being born with female-appearing external genitalia. The child has testes and no uterus. During puberty, the voice deepens, muscle mass increases, and the phallus enlarges. Serum testosterone is normal for a pubertal male, but dihydrotestosterone is markedly decreased.
item.lead_in: Impaired activity of which of the following biochemical reactions most directly explains this disorder?

options.B: Androgen-receptor complex → binding of regulatory DNA sequences
options.C: Anti-Müllerian hormone → activation of its receptor on Müllerian duct cells
options.D: Migration of GnRH-producing neurons from the developing nose to the forebrain
options.E: RET receptor activation → downstream growth and differentiation signaling

explanation.key_explanation: Steroid 5-alpha-reductase 2 converts testosterone to the more potent androgen DHT in reproductive tissues. DHT is critical for male external genital development before birth. Pubertal increases in testosterone can produce substantial virilization despite low DHT.

distractor_explanations.A: Correct. SRD5A2 deficiency reduces conversion of testosterone to DHT.
distractor_explanations.B: This describes androgen-receptor signaling; androgen-receptor loss would cause androgen insensitivity rather than isolated low DHT.
distractor_explanations.C: AMH signaling controls Müllerian regression; the absent uterus indicates this pathway functioned.
distractor_explanations.D: GnRH-neuron migration failure causes Kallmann syndrome and low gonadotropins/sex steroids rather than normal testosterone with low DHT.
distractor_explanations.E: RET is a growth-factor receptor proto-oncogene and is unrelated to testosterone-to-DHT conversion.

explanation.educational_objective: Identify steroid 5-alpha-reductase 2 as the enzyme that converts testosterone to DHT, which is required for male external genital differentiation before birth.

evidence_map.claim: SRD5A2 encodes steroid 5-alpha-reductase 2, which converts testosterone to DHT.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Explains low DHT, undervirilized external genitalia at birth, and pubertal virilization from testosterone.

evidence_map.claim: AR complexes bind DNA and regulate androgen-responsive genes; AR dysfunction causes androgen insensitivity.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: DHT production itself would not be selectively low from AR dysfunction.

evidence_map.claim: AMH/AMHR2 signaling causes Müllerian duct regression.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Absent uterus indicates Müllerian regression occurred.

evidence_map.claim: Failed olfactory/GnRH-neuron migration causes Kallmann syndrome.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Would produce central hypogonadism rather than normal pubertal testosterone.

evidence_map.claim: RET encodes a transmembrane tyrosine kinase receptor involved in growth and differentiation signaling.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Unrelated to DHT biosynthesis.

item.vignette: A 29-year-old woman is found to have medullary thyroid carcinoma after evaluation of a thyroid nodule. Biochemical testing also shows elevated plasma free metanephrines. Her father underwent thyroidectomy for medullary thyroid carcinoma at age 31. Germline testing identifies a pathogenic variant in RET.
item.lead_in: Which of the following molecular effects of the mutant protein most directly promotes tumor formation in this syndrome?

options.A: Loss of menin tumor-suppressor activity after inactivation of both MEN1 alleles in a cell
options.B: Reduced p27 tumor-suppressor activity due to CDKN1B loss of function
options.C: Failure of androgen-responsive gene transcription due to loss of androgen-receptor function
options.D: Reduced adrenal 11-beta-hydroxylase activity with accumulation of steroid precursors
options.E: Ligand-independent activation of a transmembrane receptor tyrosine kinase and its downstream growth signaling

explanation.key_explanation: MEN2 is caused by activating germline RET variants. RET encodes a transmembrane receptor in the tyrosine kinase family. MEN2-associated mutations make RET overactive so it can transmit proliferative signals without normal growth-factor stimulation.

distractor_explanations.A: MEN1 is a distinct syndrome caused by loss of the menin tumor suppressor and a second somatic hit in susceptible cells.
distractor_explanations.B: CDKN1B loss reduces p27 and causes MEN4, not MEN2.
distractor_explanations.C: AR loss causes androgen insensitivity and does not explain medullary thyroid carcinoma plus pheochromocytoma.
distractor_explanations.D: CYP11B1 deficiency causes congenital adrenal hyperplasia rather than hereditary endocrine tumors.
distractor_explanations.E: Correct. RET gain of function drives ligand-independent tyrosine-kinase signaling and uncontrolled growth.

explanation.educational_objective: Distinguish MEN2 as an autosomal-dominant gain-of-function RET proto-oncogene disorder characterized by constitutive receptor tyrosine-kinase signaling.

evidence_map.claim: RET is a transmembrane tyrosine-kinase-family receptor, and MEN2 mutations produce overactive signaling without normal ligand stimulation.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Explains hereditary medullary thyroid carcinoma and pheochromocytoma.

evidence_map.claim: MEN1 is caused by loss of menin tumor-suppressor function with a second cellular hit.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Mechanism belongs to MEN1, not RET-associated MEN2.

evidence_map.claim: CDKN1B variants reduce p27 tumor-suppressor function and cause MEN4.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Wrong MEN syndrome and gene.

evidence_map.claim: AR loss impairs androgen-responsive transcription and causes androgen insensitivity.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Does not cause the MEN2 tumor pattern.

evidence_map.claim: CYP11B1 deficiency causes 11-beta-hydroxylase-deficient congenital adrenal hyperplasia.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Not a hereditary medullary thyroid carcinoma/pheochromocytoma syndrome.

item.vignette: An 8-year-old girl is evaluated for rapid growth, premature pubic hair, acne, and progressive clitoral enlargement. Blood pressure is 152/94 mm Hg. Serum potassium is decreased, plasma renin activity is suppressed, and cortisol is decreased. Adrenal androgen concentrations and 11-deoxycortisol are elevated.
item.lead_in: Which of the following pathophysiologic changes most directly accounts for the combination of virilization and hypertension in this patient?

options.A: 21-hydroxylase deficiency causing impaired aldosterone synthesis and renal sodium loss
options.B: 17-alpha-hydroxylase deficiency causing reduced sex-steroid synthesis and increased mineralocorticoid production
options.C: 11-beta-hydroxylase deficiency causing precursor accumulation, androgen shunting, and increased salt retention
options.D: Androgen-receptor loss of function causing failure of androgen-responsive gene transcription

item.tested_construct: Biochemical and physiologic mechanism of 11-beta-hydroxylase-deficient CAH

explanation.key_explanation: CYP11B1 deficiency decreases 11-beta-hydroxylase activity. Reduced cortisol increases ACTH drive, steroid precursors accumulate and are shunted toward androgens, and precursors in the corticosterone/mineralocorticoid pathway promote sodium retention, causing low-renin hypertension. Thus virilization plus hypertension is characteristic.

distractor_explanations.A: Classic salt-wasting 21-hydroxylase deficiency reduces aldosterone and causes sodium loss rather than low-renin hypertension.
distractor_explanations.B: 17-alpha-hydroxylase deficiency causes hypertension but reduces sex-steroid production, so it does not explain virilization from androgen excess.
distractor_explanations.C: Correct. CYP11B1 deficiency produces excess androgens plus precursor-mediated salt retention and hypertension.
distractor_explanations.D: Androgen-receptor loss causes androgen resistance, not virilization with adrenal precursor accumulation and hypertension.
distractor_explanations.E: 5-alpha-reductase deficiency affects DHT-dependent sexual differentiation and does not cause adrenal androgen excess or mineralocorticoid hypertension.

explanation.educational_objective: Differentiate 11-beta-hydroxylase deficiency from other disorders of sexual development by the combined presence of androgen excess and low-renin hypertension from accumulated adrenal steroid precursors.

evidence_map.claim: CYP11B1 deficiency causes androgen excess and buildup of precursors that increase salt retention and hypertension.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Explains virilization plus hypertension, low potassium, low renin, low cortisol, and high 11-deoxycortisol.

evidence_map.claim: Severe 21-hydroxylase deficiency impairs cortisol/aldosterone synthesis and can cause salt wasting.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Opposite blood-pressure/volume phenotype from low-renin hypertension.

evidence_map.claim: CYP17A1 deficiency produces hypertension/hypokalemia but impairs sex-hormone production.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Hypertension fits, virilization from androgen excess does not.

evidence_map.claim: AR loss produces androgen insensitivity.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Cannot explain androgen-driven virilization and adrenal steroid precursor abnormalities.

evidence_map.claim: SRD5A2 deficiency reduces testosterone-to-DHT conversion and affects external genital development.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Does not cause adrenal precursor excess or mineralocorticoid hypertension.
